summary:
Podcast show notes for episode 385 of Eptura's Workplace Innovator, hosted by Mike Petrusky, featuring Vik Bangia, MCR, CEO of Verum Consulting and Verum's OutsourceUSA. Bangia is described as a corporate real estate (CRE) and facilities management (FM) outsourcing advisor and workplace strategist, and author of "Tales from an Accidental Corporate Real Estate Leader".

The conversation opens with the two reflecting on time spent together at IFMA's World Workplace in Minneapolis, then looks ahead to a new year framed around challenges and opportunities for the profession. The central theme is how facilities management leaders can use AI to free up capacity for more strategic thinking. The argument advanced is that AI can absorb mundane and routine tasks in the built environment, allowing FM leaders to move up the value chain rather than staying in reactive execution.

Bangia also recounts his own career journey in corporate real estate as a way of encouraging listeners to build awareness of AI's current capabilities and to adopt new tools rather than wait. A further point of emphasis is the role of outsourcing relationships and third-party service providers in delivering AI-enabled capability, since much FM work is delivered through vendors; the pair offer real world examples of how these relationships can be used to leverage AI.

The notes close with standard promotional links: LinkedIn profiles for Bangia and Petrusky, the Verum Consulting site, Eptura's podcast resource hub with past interviews and free resources, the Eptura corporate site, and a YouTube playlist for the full video version.

No statistics, survey data, or quantified claims are included in the show notes. There is no discussion of desk booking, hot desking, visitor management, return-to-office mandates, or workplace analytics metrics; the content is a high-level strategic and AI-adoption conversation aimed at FM and CRE practitioners.

claims.claim: AI has the potential to take over mundane and routine tasks in the built environment, freeing FM leaders to think more strategically
claims.attribution: Vik Bangia, CEO of Verum Consulting, on Eptura's Workplace Innovator podcast

claims.claim: Outsourcing relationships and service providers are essential to leveraging AI in facilities management
Vik Bangia is the author of "Tales from an Accidental Corporate Real Estate Leader"
